title: Completion answers three positions as the position around them.
text: Three cursor positions get the list of the position that contains them, which `rule:ide/completion-offers-only-what-the-compiler-derived` does not allow. The receiver half of an access is one: `$u<|>->name` is writing a variable, and the variables in scope are not offered (`tests/lsp/completion/a-cursor-in-the-receiver-half-is-not-asking-for-members.lspt`). A written type that the tokens do not give away is another: a property's type, and a type argument between `<` and `>`. The inside of a string literal is the third, where the statement keywords are offered beside the variables an interpolation takes (`tests/lsp/completion/a-string-literal-is-a-statement-position.lspt`).
